title: Ernie Andrews in Milan, "I'll See You Later, So Long," and predicting Rickie Lee Jones
summary: Callender hopes Andrews will record his song with Mary Lou's lyric and tells of predicting a hit for Rickie Lee Jones at a Warner date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: He just got back from Italy or something.

Italy. Milano. He was at a Jazz concert, a Jazz festival, the Thad Jones Big Band. He didn't get to sing with the big band, because...he mentioned the guy's name who was singing with the band. So he did his set with a smaller group. But yeah, Ernie's going to make it. And I have another that he's going to do later, too, called, 'I'll See You Later, So Long.'
Oh, the one that Mary Lou...
Mary Lou wrote a lyric to. It started out as 'Dolphin Street Boogie.' It started out as a theme on the station. Well, you heard.
Yes, at your concert.
Right, the girls all played it. She's got a wild lyric to it. So I'm sure Ernie would...this will suit him. It might even be a hit for him.
That would be nice.

I have predicted a few hits. For instance, a few years ago I was on a date with Rickie Lee Jones. They called me to put a bass line and a tuba line for some things she had done. This was for Warner's. I said, 'This girl is going to be a hit.' And she is.
It will. It will happen big. All he has to do is to stay healthy.
